proposal.utterance: Classify 'Abusus' (the right of abuse, in Roman-law property theory) in BFO terms.

entities.label: Abusus
entities.rationale: Abusus (ius abutendi) is the right to alienate, consume, or destroy property — one of the three classical sticks of Roman dominium (usus, fructus, abusus). As a right, it is a specifically dependent continuant that inheres in a legal person qua owner; it is externally grounded in the legal system's recognition of ownership rather than in any intrinsic property of the bearer, making Role (BFO_0000023) the correct type. It is modeled as a class (a kind of legal right) rather than an individual because it designates a general category of right that can be instantiated by many owners. It is a subclass of working:LegalRight, which is already typed as BFO_0000023.

relations.rationale: Abusus is a species of legal right (ius in rem), and LegalRight is already established in the working ontology as a Role (BFO_0000023). SubclassOf expresses the genus-species relationship.

open_questions: Should Abusus be further distinguished from Usus (right of use) and Fructus (right to fruits)? If so, shall we mint Usus and Fructus as sibling subclasses of LegalRight, and introduce a class 'DominalRight' or 'IusInRem' as their common parent under LegalRight?

Roman dominium is the canonical bearer of Abusus. Shall we introduce a class 'Dominium' (ownership role) as a separate Role class to which Abusus is relationally tied (e.g., via a part-of or dependency relation), or is it sufficient to rely on the general LegalRight hierarchy?

Should Abusus be modeled with a disposition component (BFO_0000016) to capture the latent capacity to alienate or destroy, distinct from its exercise as a process? Or is the Role typing sufficient for present purposes?
Is the scope intended to be specifically Roman law (historical), or should Abusus serve as a cross-jurisdictional archetype for 'alienation right' in property theory generally?
proposal.rationale_summary: Abusus is the Roman-law component of full ownership (dominium) that authorises the owner to alienate, encumber, consume, or destroy the thing owned. Ontologically it is a specifically dependent continuant: it cannot exist without a bearer (the owner) and it is grounded externally in legal-institutional recognition rather than in any physical property of the bearer, which classifies it as a Role (BFO_0000023) rather than a Quality or Disposition. It is best introduced as a class (a kind of right) rather than an individual, because many distinct property-holding persons can each instantiate an Abusus. Placing it as a subclass of the existing working:LegalRight class (itself typed BFO_0000023) captures the genus-species relationship cleanly and reuses existing ontological commitments. No new top-level BFO type is required.
